cards.text: The LORD has told Moses, Israel's leader, that the time of his death is near (Deuteronomy 31:14). Now Moses recites a song to the whole assembly of Israel, from beginning to end, and his first line calls on the heavens and the earth to listen. Friend, when your opening line is addressed to the SKY, everybody in the room sits up straight.

cards.question: Moses wants his teaching to land soft, the way something settles on new grass. What does he want his words to be like?

cards.text: Then Moses says he will proclaim the name of the LORD, and he gives God a name that's SOLID. Doesn't move, doesn't crack, doesn't wear down like my edges did after years of stamping.

cards.question: Moses gives God a solid name. He calls Him the ___.

cards.text: His work is perfect, and all His ways are just. But then the song turns: His people have acted corruptly toward Him, a perverse and crooked generation.

cards.question: Moses asks if this is how they repay the LORD. What does he say the LORD is to them?

cards.text: Then Moses tells them to remember the days of old, and to ask their fathers and their elders, who will tell them. Friend, ask ME about my years stuck in a junk drawer and you'd better clear your whole afternoon.
Then the song looks back to when the Most High gave the nations their inheritance and set the boundaries of the peoples. The LORD had a portion of His own.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD's own portion is His people, Jacob.
Moses sings about how the LORD found His people, Jacob. Where did He find him?

cards.text: There He surrounded him, instructed him and guarded him as the apple of His eye. Then Moses paints a picture: an eagle stirring up its nest and hovering over its young.

cards.question: In Moses' picture, the LORD is like that eagle. He spread His ___ to catch them.
Moses says the LORD had help from foreign gods when He led His people.

cards.text: Then Moses sings that the LORD fed them, even with honey from the rock and oil from the flinty crag. Food out of solid stone, friend, that's like reaching into an EMPTY cookie jar and pulling out a fresh batch.

cards.question: Moses lists curds, milk, lambs, wheat and grapes, and he says they were only plain and simple food.

cards.text: Then Jeshurun, a name the song uses here for God's people, grew fat and kicked. Bloated and gorged, like me after one too many test batches, except I don't kick, I just lie there on my gold base and groan.

cards.question: Full and bloated, Jeshurun ___ the God who made him.

cards.text: Honey from a ROCK, and they went looking for other gods. They provoked God's jealousy with foreign gods and enraged Him with abominations.

cards.question: Moses says Israel sacrificed to ___, not to God.
Moses says the gods Israel turned to were old gods.

cards.text: Moses tells them they ignored the Rock who brought them forth and forgot the God who gave them birth. When the LORD saw this, He rejected them.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD rejected His people when He saw what they did. Who provoked Him to anger?
The LORD says He will hide His face from His people.

cards.text: He calls them children of unfaithfulness. They made Him jealous with what is not God, with worthless idols, so He turns it right back around on them.

cards.question: Israel made God jealous with what is not God. How does God say He'll make them jealous?

answers.text: By those who aren't even a people
By those who lead His own people
By those who serve at His altar

cards.text: God says a fire has been kindled by His anger, and it burns to the depths of Sheol. He says He'll heap disasters on them: hunger, plague, wild beasts, vipers, the sword outside and terror inside.
Then God says He would have said He'd cut them to pieces and blot out their memory from mankind. But there's an if.

cards.question: What held God back from blotting out the memory of His people?

answers.text: Their enemies would take the credit
Moses would beg Him to stop
Israel would turn back to Him

cards.text: Moses says Israel has no understanding, and if only they were wise, they'd see where this is heading. Then he asks: how could one man chase a THOUSAND, or two put ten thousand to flight?

cards.question: One man chasing a thousand. What does Moses say is the only way that could happen?

answers.text: The LORD had given them up
Their army had grown too small
Their weapons had grown too old

cards.text: Moses says their rock is not like our Rock, and even the enemies admit it. And their vine is from the vine of Sodom and the fields of Gomorrah, cities the LORD rained fire on (Genesis 19:24), and friend, that is NOT a vineyard you put on the label.

cards.question: From that vine, the grapes are ___ and the clusters are bitter.

cards.text: Their wine is the venom of serpents, the deadly poison of cobras. Then God speaks again: "Have I not stored up these things, sealed up within My vaults?"

cards.question: God says vengeance belongs to His people.

cards.text: God says their foot will slip and their doom is coming quickly. Then the song turns toward hope: the LORD will vindicate His people.

cards.question: The LORD will have compassion on His servants. When?

answers.text: When He sees their strength is gone
When they win their next battle
When they bring a bigger offering

cards.text: The LORD will ask where their gods are now, the ones that ate the fat of their sacrifices, and tell them to rise up and help. I picture them like the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with, swearing they've STILL got a little charge left.

cards.question: God says there are other gods besides Him, but He is the greatest.
God brings death and gives life, and He wounds and heals. He says there is ___ who can deliver from His hand.

cards.text: Then God lifts up His hand to heaven and makes a declaration. Friend, when GOD raises His hand to declare something, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: When God lifts His hand to heaven and declares, what does He say His words are as sure as?

cards.text: God says when He sharpens His flashing sword, He will repay those who hate Him. And then the song ends with a call to rejoice.

cards.question: At the end of the song, Moses calls on the ___ to rejoice with God's people.

cards.text: Moses calls the heavens to rejoice and all God's angels to worship Him, and he sings that God will cleanse His land and His people. That's the whole song, friend, but this story isn't done yet, so keep that apron on.
